scenarios.name: Request is mechanical
given: A request to create or extend a utility script
when: The operation's input/output is fully determined by rules and data
The operation is idempotent (running twice produces the same result)
No domain knowledge beyond the input data is required
then: Proceed with implementation

scenarios.name: Request is semantic
given: A request to create or extend a utility script
when: The operation requires understanding meaning, quality, or fitness
then: Reject the request
Explain why the task requires LLM judgment
Suggest the caller handle it in the skill's LLM layer (prompt instructions or subagent)

scenarios.name: Request is practice-specific
given: A request to create a utility script
when: The script would only work for one specific practice, method, or baseline
then: Reject the request
Suggest either generalizing the approach or handling it as a one-off in the skill's workflow

scenarios.name: Hardcoded data should be externalized
given: A utility script contains practice-specific constants, mappings, or IDs
when: The data could be provided via a config file or command-line argument
then: Externalize the data into a `--config` or `--assignments` JSON file
The script's logic remains general-purpose

scenarios.name: New utility follows conventions
given: A new utility script is created
then: It uses `argparse` with `--help`
It imports from `utils/_shared.py` where applicable
It uses `--fix` for write operations
It follows kebab-case naming: `verb-noun.py`
It includes a docstring with purpose and usage examples

scenarios.name: Extended utility preserves interfaces
then: All existing CLI arguments and flags still work identically
New functionality is added as new flags or modes

scenarios.name: The reuse ladder is climbed in order
given: A mechanical need has been confirmed
then: The first rung that fully solves it is taken, in this order:
A new script is only written when rungs 1–4 genuinely do not reach

scenarios.name: Laziness applies to the solution, never the change
given: A utility is created or extended
then: Every caller, skill reference, and `utils/README.md` entry the change touches is updated
These are never cut to save effort: schema validation, cross-reference integrity checks, error handling that would lose a generated artifact, anything the user asked for

scenarios.name: A deliberate shortcut names its ceiling
given: A simpler implementation is chosen that will not hold in every case
then: A comment records it as `shortcut: <the limit>, <when to upgrade>`
The limit and the upgrade trigger are both stated, because a marker with no trigger is the one that rots
The ledger is one grep, so no script or skill is added to collect it:

scenarios.name: Registry updated after changes
given: A utility was created, extended, or removed
then: `utils/README.md` reflects the change
New scripts appear in the appropriate section
Removed scripts are no longer listed
